base.description: the resolved base ref the diff was taken from

languages.description: canonical language names present in the changed CODE files, most-changed first

by_language.description: the same changed files, grouped by the language each is WRITTEN IN. One entry per name in `languages`, spelled identically. A code file belongs to exactly one entry; a file no lens should own (docs, lockfiles) belongs to none.

language.description: one of the names in `languages`, verbatim

files.description: changed paths written in this language, repo-relative, exactly as they appear in `files`

has_code.description: false when every changed file is docs/config/build only

concurrency.description: true only if the diff actually adds/changes goroutines, threads, async, locks, shared mutable state or transactions

performance.description: true only if the diff actually adds/changes I/O, queries, loops over unbounded input, allocation in hot paths, or a benchmark exists to measure against

tests_changed.description: true if any test file changed

summary.description: two sentences on what this change set does, for the lenses

mechanical_ran.description: true only if `clerk lint` actually executed; false when the command does not exist

mechanical.description: findings from `clerk lint`, verbatim; empty when it ran and found nothing

id.description: stable kebab-case id, unique within this review

severity.description: honest impact, graded on what the defect COSTS and not on how central it is to your lens: high = a wrong or lost outcome for a user or caller in normal operation, or a security or data-integrity failure; medium = a real but bounded or conditional cost — degraded behaviour under load, a wrong result on an edge path, or a test that cannot fail for the behaviour it names; low = no runtime symptom and no operational cost — a convention, a name, a comment, a redundant test; never inflated to force attention

claim.description: one sentence stating the defect, precise enough to reproduce if runtime

nature.description: runtime = an independent agent could demonstrate it by executing code; quality = a convention/structure/test defect with no runtime symptom

failure_scenario.description: concrete inputs/state -> wrong output, for runtime findings

note.description: what you deliberately did NOT flag and why, when that is the informative part

clusters.description: every finding id exactly once across all clusters; a finding with no duplicate is a cluster of one

ids.description: the finding ids that are all the SAME defect

why.description: for clusters of more than one: what the single underlying defect is

refuted.description: true when you ran something and it did NOT establish the defect is real

blocked.description: true when you could not execute the check at all — a missing dependency, an absent toolchain, an unreachable service. Not a refutation: nothing was tested.

basis.description: for a runtime claim: the exact command run and the raw output tail. For a quality claim: the specific rule and the line it is violated at.

severity_after.description: your own severity once you looked; null to keep the reviewer's

lens.description: the lens key that raised this, verbatim from the survivor list; when deduplicating two lenses into one finding, join their keys with " + "

confidence.description: confirmed = reproduced by execution, or a quality rule cited at a specific line

evidence.description: the command + output that reproduced it, or the rule + line

coverage_gaps.description: what this audit could NOT judge and why — an unrun modality, a file nobody read, a claim nobody could test
